articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Vision, and Audio
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can jointly process code repositories, visual diagrams, and spoken instructions in a single inference pass. Benchmarks show a 38% improvement on SWE-bench and near-human performance on graduate-level scientific reasoning tasks. The model also introduces a persistent memory architecture that maintains coherent context across sessions.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2, which solved 89% of International Mathematical Olympiad problems from the past decade, surpassing the previous record of 74%. The system uses a novel chain-of-verification approach where multiple specialized reasoning modules cross-check each other's proofs. This marks a significant step toward AI systems capable of genuine mathematical discovery rather than pattern matching.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Unveils Atlas Gen 3 with Dexterous Manipulation for Warehouse Logistics
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics demonstrated the third-generation Atlas humanoid robot performing complex warehouse pick-and-pack operations with 99.2% accuracy across diverse object geometries. The system leverages a transformer-based visuomotor policy trained on 50,000 hours of teleoperation data combined with sim-to-real transfer. Commercial deployments with DHL and Amazon are slated to begin in Q1 2027.

articles.title: Figure AI's Humanoid Robot Completes Full 8-Hour Shift at BMW Manufacturing Plant
articles.summary: Figure AI reported that its Figure 03 humanoid robot successfully completed consecutive unsupervised 8-hour shifts on a BMW assembly line in Spartanburg, South Carolina, handling door panel installation and quality inspection. The robot uses on-device large language model reasoning to interpret ambiguous assembly instructions and adapt to part variations in real time. This milestone represents the first commercially viable full-shift deployment of a general-purpose humanoid in automotive manufacturing.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional AI Oversight Framework Adopted by EU AI Office
articles.summary: Anthropic published a formal Constitutional AI oversight protocol that the EU AI Office has adopted as a reference framework for auditing frontier AI systems under the EU AI Act. The framework includes automated red-teaming pipelines, interpretability checkpoints, and mandatory capability evaluations at defined compute thresholds. This represents the first time a major AI lab's internal safety methodology has been codified into regulatory guidance.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm GAA Process Node for Next-Gen AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed volume production on its N1.4 gate-all-around (GAA) transistor process, which delivers a 25% performance uplift and 35% power reduction over its 2nm node. The first customers include NVIDIA and Apple, with AI accelerator chips expected to reach hyperscalers by mid-2027. The node supports up to 400 billion transistor designs on a single reticle, enabling a new class of monolithic AI training chips.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuit with 48 Logical Qubits
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum jointly demonstrated a fault-tolerant quantum computation using 48 logical qubits with error rates below the threshold needed for practical quantum advantage in certain optimization problems. The system ran a materials science simulation that would take classical supercomputers an estimated 300 years. While general-purpose quantum computing remains years away, this result validates the viability of error-corrected quantum systems for specific scientific workloads.

articles.title: Toyota Research Institute Deploys Fleet of 100 Autonomous Vehicles in Dense Urban Tokyo Traffic
articles.summary: Toyota Research Institute launched a 100-vehicle autonomous fleet operating Level 4 self-driving in central Tokyo's congested Shibuya and Shinjuku districts without safety drivers. The system uses a combination of lidar, radar, and a vision-language model that interprets ambiguous traffic scenarios including unmarked intersections and pedestrian-dense crosswalks. Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism approved the deployment under a new regulatory sandbox framework.
